methodological_rigor.justification: A multi-institutional radiomics pilot using a purpose-built 3D-printed phantom scanned 10 times on each of five MR systems (1.5T Philips Unity, 1.5T GE Artist, 1.5T Siemens Sola, 1.5T Philips Ingenia, two 0.35T ViewRay MRIdian). Pyradiomics feature extraction, CV, and ICC(3,1) for agreement are appropriate methods. The stability-of-phantom-contents experiment with vitamin D capsules (26 weeks, control vs test) is a strength. Limitations: only one phantom unit built (no inter-phantom variability), contouring approach keeps shape constant across scans (authors acknowledge shape-feature stability is artificially inflated), each scanner scanned once at one institution with different time-interval structures across sites, and no formal blinded analysis pipeline. No correction for multiple comparisons across 107 features x multiple scanners x 2 sequences.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: MRI radiomics reproducibility is a critical prerequisite for deploying imaging biomarkers in oncology multi-institutional trials, especially for MR-linac workflows. The pilot identifies features that are consistent across scanners (e.g., Glcm Idmn and Idn) and demonstrates that TrueFISP on ViewRay has good inter-scanner correlation. However, this is a phantom-only technical study with no patient outcome linkage; translational path to clinical biomarker deployment is indirect. LoE 5 (basic/technical science).

reporting_quality.justification: Although the manuscript mentions PyRadiomics and IBSI compliance, full IBSI reporting is not explicitly documented. Methods describe phantom design, scanner models, bin width (64 fixed), GLCM symmetry, and ICC calculations with acceptable detail. Missing elements: no data or code availability statement, no public deposit of the phantom CAD files or raw feature data, limited description of how image registration was performed for the 'one segmentation set' reuse across image sets, and no pre-specified analysis plan. Figure 6 panels A/B/C legends appear duplicated with near-identical wording.

novelty_literature.justification: Radiomic phantom reproducibility studies have been published by multiple groups (Lee 2021, Rai 2020, Ericsson-Szecsenyi 2022, Cheong 2024, Hajianfar 2024), many of which the authors cite. The novel contributions here are (1) a purpose-built 3D-printed phantom with grid and egg-shape geometries including vitamin D3 capsules in olive oil, (2) inclusion of MR-linac systems (Unity and ViewRay), and (3) cross-vendor comparison at 1.5T plus 0.35T. Incremental but technically useful addition to the field.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is readable but has notable defects: Figure 6A/B/C legends are repeated verbatim; Equations for CV and ICC are referenced ('by (29)' and 'by (43)') but not displayed as properly formatted equations in the text; some sentences are ungrammatical ('with/without 20% wood particles'); internal inconsistency: methods state 'No appreciable changes... over 12 weeks' while the experiment tracked 26 weeks. Figures are systematically described but quantitative summary tables beyond the heat map are limited.

key_strengths: Purpose-built 3D-printed MR-safe phantom with multiple geometries (grids and eggs) and tissue-mimicking vitamin D capsules in olive oil
Four-institution multi-vendor scan campaign including both 1.5T systems and 0.35T MR-linac ViewRay platforms
Phantom stability verified over 26 weeks with control vs test capsule diameter/weight measurements
ICC(3,1) used to identify features with robust cross-scanner correlation (TrueFISP 80/107 features above ICC 0.9)
key_concerns: Only one phantom unit built; inter-phantom reproducibility not assessed
Shape-feature stability is inflated because the same contour was reused across all scans (authors acknowledge this)
No multiple-comparison correction across 107 features x scanners x sequences
Figure 6A/B/C legends duplicated; 12-week vs 26-week stability statement inconsistency
No data, code, or CAD-file availability statement despite reproducibility emphasis
No patient-data validation linking robust features to clinical outcomes
chief_reviewer.rationale: A useful technical pilot for MR radiomics reproducibility with a novel 3D-printed phantom, but limited by single-phantom design, shape-feature confound, and presentation defects, placing it in Tier 3 with minor revisions.
